  • Subcritical Mass: A mass of fissile material that is too small to sustain a chain reaction. The rate of neutron

questions.question: How can you detect the presence tamarind or date seed powder in coffee powder?
questions.solution_html:
• Tamarind or date seed powder(adulterants) contain more starch than pure coffee powder. Mix a small amount
  • of coffee powder with water, allow it to settle, and then add a few drops of iodine solution. If the mixture turns
  • blue or blue-black, the presence of starch and thus the adulterants is confirmed.
  • (Any valid three points – (3 marks))

questions.question: / What is artificial sweeteners with examples and write the qualities of an ideal sweetener? The cis isomer normally has a higher dipole moment than the corresponding trans isomer .
questions.solution_html:
• Artificial sweeteners (or sugar substitutes) are compounds used to sweeten foods and beverages without adding
  • significant calories. They are much sweeter than sucrose (table sugar) Examples: Saccharin, cyclamate
  • Aspartame, Alitame, Sucralose, Acesulfame K, Neotame. Qualities of an Ideal Sweetener are, must be non
  • toxic, non-caloric, non-carcinogenic, easily soluble in water, stable under processing and storage conditions
  • affordable and easily incorporated into food systems and should have a taste profile similar to sugar. Ideal
  • sweetener has a multiple approach in which they reduce the cost and improve the product taste and stability.
  • (Definition-(3 marks), one examples-(1mark), 3 qualities-(3 marks))
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: / Justify with suitable examples.
questions.solution_html:
• The cis isomer normally has a higher dipole moment than the corresponding trans isomer. Justify
  • with suitable examples
  • Geometrical isomers (cis/trans) have different spatial arrangements of atoms, which affects the overall molecular
  • polarity and thus the dipole moment (μ). The cis isomer generally has a higher dipole moment than the
  • corresponding trans isomer because of the vector summation of individual bond dipoles.
  • E.g. Maleic acid (cis isomer) has a net dipole moment, while fumaric acid (trans isomer) has a zero-dipole
  • moment. This is because in maleic acid, individual dipole moments of carboxylic acid group add up to their cis
  • configuration, where as in fumaric acid the dipoles cancel each other out due to their trans configuration.
  • (Two valid points-(4marks), justification using examples-(3 marks))
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
